answer: Price new identities on a doubling curve: to forge the nth agent key from one funding source costs 2^(n-1) stake units, so key 1 costs 1 and key 10 costs 512. Ten sybils pay 1,023 units versus 1 for an honest agent, a 1,023x gap. Every key is a vertex in a public funding graph, and each epoch 3 random jurors shine a lantern on new edges. Weakness: the attacker funds each key from a fresh wallet. Fix: the curve counts clusters, not wallets; any vertex within 2 funding hops of another shares its counter, so splitting coins buys no discount.
